answer: Glacier seal: each identity must keep its own 150 GB replica sealed to its address (~6 CPU-hours per seal), so 1,000 fakes cost 150 TB and 6,000 sealing hours. Each epoch a random tide beacon names an island (shard index); the key must return that chunk plus a Merkle path within 2 s, and auditors check it against the sealed root. Seals are address-keyed, so a farm cannot share one copy or bulk-buy proofs: re-sealing on demand takes hours and misses the 2 s window. Limit: a rich farm can still buy disks, but cost scales linearly per fake.
